block_05_direct_answer.title: Direct answer
block_05_direct_answer.body_html: A floor plan should be judged by usable space, not only total area. For payment-plan buyers, check room proportions, circulation, storage, natural light, privacy, balcony usability, furniture placement and any wasted or awkward space. Compare plans at similar sizes because two units with the same area can function very differently.

items.answer: A floor plan should be judged by usable space, not only total area. For payment-plan buyers, look beyond total area and check how much space is practically usable once circulation, columns, balconies and service areas are considered.
items.question: What should I check in a floor plan?

items.answer: Unit size should be compared through usable space and layout efficiency, not area alone. Check corridors, room proportions, columns, balconies and circulation so a larger headline area is not automatically treated as the better layout.
items.question: How should I compare unit sizes?

items.answer: Apartments and villas suit different budgets, lifestyles, maintenance needs and buyer goals. Check service charges, maintenance and upkeep because operating costs can differ materially between apartments, villas and communities.
items.question: Which is better: an apartment or a villa?

items.answer: A view premium is justified only when the view is durable and valued by future buyers. Consider service charges, maintenance exposure and other recurring costs that may accompany premium waterfront facilities or locations.
items.question: How should I assess whether a view premium is justified?

items.answer: Project location should be judged at street and access level, not only by district name. The project sits in a less convenient or less desirable part of an otherwise attractive area. Verify the exact location because two projects in the same area can offer very different day-to-day quality.
